title: [torch.compile] Significantly speed up cold start times
body:
Previously, the vLLM-compile compilation:
1. does a full dynamo trace to get a full graph
2. splits the graph on attention ops into N subgraphs
3. compiles each of the N subgraphs via standalone_compile.
4. If any of the subgraphs are the same, we rely on aotautograd and inductor to cache-hit, but we still end up producing N artifacts total. Usually there are 3 unique graphs in vLLM models.
5. vLLM stores a mapping of N subgraph indices to N compiled artifacts.

Taking control of this back into vLLM's hands significantly improves cold start time. That is, instead of storing a mapping from N subgraph indices to N compiled artifacts, we instead store a mapping from the subgraph hash to compiled artifact, so we end up making only unique compiled artifacts.

Commit `34ddf135fd` introduced `recursive_replace()` in `TransformersBase`, which replaced every HF `*RMSNorm` module with SGLang's `sgl_kernel.rmsnorm`. ## Motivation

Fixes #40903.

On the DeepSeek chunked-prefix MHA path, `_chunked_prefix_attn_mha` merges per-chunk attention states with `merge_state` (`merge_state_v2` / Triton), which expects natural-log LSE. The flashinfer ragged prefill wrapper (`BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`) and `trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek` return base-2 LSE, and nothing converts in between. So on every prefix-cache hit that reaches the merge, the long cached prefix is over-weighted relative to the new tokens.

## Purpose

Fixes #55350.

Kimi-K3's low-token-count TP8 KDA projection-overlap path fails during CUDA
graph profiling on H100/SM90a. Two independent incompatibilities are involved:

1. the skinny N/K kernels unconditionally emit PTX `fma.f32.bf16`, which
   requires SM100 or newer and fails libNVVM compilation for `sm_90a`; and
2. FlashInfer's `cute-dsl` QKVG backend rejects SM90 during backend validation.

PR #55108 avoids the failure by disabling KDA projection overlap on Hopper.
This PR keeps the overlap structure enabled while selecting architecture-safe
operations.

title: [ROCm] Rotate even-batch decode attention grid across XCDs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #41151.

HIP assigns workgroups to XCDs round-robin. Triton decode stage-1 launches with `batch` as the fastest grid axis, so an **even** batch size parks every workgroup for a given request on a subset of XCDs. CUDA-graph padding fills unused slots with `seq_len=1`, and those empty slots still take whole XCDs — at long context the padded bs-5→8 graph was ~1.4× slower than an exact bs-5 launch on the attention kernel alone (Olmo-3-7B shapes).

When `batch % 2 == 0` on HIP, rotate the batch index by `(head + split) % batch` so work from every request is spread across XCDs. Odd batches are already interleaved by the round-robin mapping and are left alone. CUDA is unchanged.
